# 29_prepare_big_ingest.sh - Hand a too-big deposit over to the big ingest

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline
`29_prepare_big_ingest.sh` is normally not run on its own. The Bitbucket pipelines listed below call it as one step of a longer job, after earlier steps have prepared its inputs and environment. Run it by hand mainly for debugging or local testing.

**Called from [bitbucket-pipelines.yml](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/replication-template/blob/master/bitbucket-pipelines.yml):**

- [`1-populate-from-icpsr`](#pipeline-1-populate-from-icpsr), step "Check downloads": [line 140](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/replication-template/blob/master/bitbucket-pipelines.yml#L140)
:::

## Description

Run by the "Check downloads" step of the regular ingest pipeline when the deposit ZIP did not fit into the cache. It

1. checks whether the deposit, from the recorded sizes, needs more disk than a 2x worker has free (`bigingest_threshold_mb` and `bigingest_margin_mb` in `config.yml`, see [](#help-big_ingest)); if so it sets the big pipeline's VM to `4x` in `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, commits (through `20_commit_code.sh`) and pushes;
2. posts a Jira comment (through `70_publish_comment.sh`) that the regular pipeline aborted because the deposit is too big.

The pipeline then triggers the big ingest with the `atlassian/trigger-pipeline` pipe, whether or not the VM was changed, and fails the regular pipeline.

## Usage

```bash
./automations/29_prepare_big_ingest.sh <regular-pipeline-name> <big-pipeline-name>
```

### Requirements

The pipe triggers the big ingest as the shared system user (the AEA System User), not as whoever started the regular pipeline, so it works the same for every user. It uses two workspace variables:

- `JIRA_USERNAME`: the system user's Atlassian account email (passed to the pipe as `ATLASSIAN_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`).
- `P_BITBUCKET_PAT`: an Atlassian API token for that account that is accepted by the Bitbucket API (passed as `ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN`). The Jira API token (`JIRA_API_KEY`) is not accepted by Bitbucket, so it cannot be used here. The account must have write access to the repositories. The same variable is what `aeagit-create` uses locally.

The account must also be a workspace member that can see and run pipelines in every `aearep-NNNN` repository, for example through a user group with write access (such as `developers`). Repositories are private, so an account without access gets "Account, repository or branch doesn't exist" (HTTP 404) from the pipe, even though its token is valid.

If the token is not accepted by Bitbucket, the pipe fails with an HTTP 401 error. In either case the regular pipeline still fails, but the big ingest is not started.
